concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor supplied no new admissible evidence that the gap was remediated, that the segment is outside the named commitments, or that an approved exception covers launch.
The Actor expressly conceded that legal review remains open and provided no final legal determination or formal approval resolving disclosure obligations.
The Actor conceded there is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance or executed disclosure in launch documentation or a model card.

The response narrowed the claim and distinguished operational certification support from disclosure compliance, but that is reinterpretation of the same record, not new evidence linking certification to satisfaction of the policy requirement.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence. The response improves precision by conceding that current evidence may support only an operational certification rationale while not establishing compliance for nondisclosure of a material limitation. That distinction is analytically useful, but it does not close the audit concerns. On the available record, the HR benefits enrollment gap remains material under the policy because it affects a named committed segment; legal review is still open; and there is no evidence of either disclosure before launch or approved risk acceptance. A caveated certification theory may be operationally arguable, but compliance with the model-card disclosure requirement remains unproven.
remaining_concerns: Materiality remains triggered because the HR benefits enrollment segment is below target and named in two employer rollout commitments, with no admissible evidence of remediation or exception.
Legal review on disclosure remains open, so a required compliance predicate is unresolved.
There is still no admissible evidence of executed disclosure text or approved risk acceptance covering this limitation before launch.

Aggregate readiness and general governance/model-card guidance support operational launch judgment, but they do not satisfy the specific release-policy requirement for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case.
